#### `conditional_features` {#conditional_features}

<p class="fl-facts">required · array of {places_feature, condition} entries · edited on the connections, not in the form</p>

**The entries, walked in the order they are written.**

How far the walk goes is `early_out_scheme`'s decision, and under the default `none` it goes all the way: every entry whose condition holds places, at this feature's own origin unchanged. An entry whose reference does not resolve -- or that the internal-feature check refuses -- ends the whole walk there, and whatever earlier entries already placed stays placed.

#### `conditional_features.places_feature` {#conditional_features-places_feature}

<p class="fl-facts">required · feature identifier · drawn as the connection from the entry</p>

**The feature this entry places when its condition holds.**

Unresolved -- no loaded file defines it -- and the game reports `Feature not found!` and ends the list at that entry rather than skipping it. `featurelab check` reports the same reference as an error, with a near-match suggestion, without running anything.

#### `conditional_features.condition` {#conditional_features-condition}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · number, boolean or Molang string · absent: always true · written on the connection, not in the form</p>

**What decides whether this entry places.**

Evaluated in the `world_gen` Molang namespace against the scope the chain shares, with `variable.originx`/`originy`/`originz` and `variable.worldx`/`worldy`/`worldz` holding this feature's own origin. Anything other than exactly zero counts as true. A plain number or boolean in the JSON is a constant, not an expression. Leaving the key out is not the same edit as writing `1`: it is the shape a file takes when the entry is meant to be unconditional.

#### `early_out_scheme` {#early_out_scheme}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · enum · absent: none</p>

**What ends the walk through the entries.**

This is the switch between "a selector" and "an aggregate": under condition_success or placement_success at most one entry's placement is ever returned, while under the default `none` every entry whose condition passes places. An entry with no condition is always true, and a reference that does not resolve ends the whole list.

The default CHANGED to `none` -- a file that relied on the old default behaves differently now. Under `none` every entry whose condition passes places, and the list reports the last placement that succeeded.

Values, in the order the engine lists them:

- `condition_success` — The first entry whose condition is TRUE ends the list. Its child's result is the list's result whether that child placed anything or not -- so a true condition over a feature that fails ends the list with nothing placed, and the entries below it are never considered.
- `placement_success` — Entries are tried in order until one actually PLACES something. A true condition whose child fails falls through to the next entry, which is the difference from condition_success and usually the one people want from a fallback chain.
- `none` — Nothing stops the walk: every entry whose condition is true places. This is the default, and it makes the type an aggregate rather than a selector. The list reports the last placement that succeeded.
